sup-45e9b39ec46a9e4c-q5:whole.hint: Compare the velocity direction with the magnetic-field direction. Only the perpendicular component is deflected.
notes: The magnetic force is |F| = |q|vB sin θ. For perpendicular circular motion, |q|vB = mv²/r, giving r = mv/(|q|B).
A magnetic field alone does no work: the force is perpendicular to velocity. Reverse the force direction for a negative charge.

sup-b1f5972664ec5178-q1:whole.hint: Identify the potential change along the particle’s actual path and keep the sign of its charge.
notes: In a uniform electric field, F = qE and a = qE/m. Across a potential change, ΔE_k = −qΔV if the electric force is the only force doing work.
Between parallel plates, |E| = |ΔV|/d away from edge effects. Do not use the entire plate-to-plate voltage for a particle that crosses only part of the gap.
